function: Joint far/near-field user classification, multi-user precoding and power allocation for downlink near-field XL-MIMO with UAV and ground users, via fine-tuned GPT-2 (pp. 5-6)
system: Downlink XL-MIMO, 256-element ULA BS serving up to 10 single-antenna UAV and ground users, no RIS, 30 GHz, BS height 15 m, tilt 5 degrees (p. 7)
method: Pretrained GPT-2 (smallest, d=768) with attention encoder and projection adapters; only addition and layer-norm layers fine-tuned; unsupervised sum-rate loss for precoding, supervised MSE for classification (pp. 5-6)
data_channel: Simulated near-field spherical-wave channel following [10], [32] (Cui and Dai; Lu and Dai); 8,000 training, 1,000 validation, 1,000 test samples, random user positions (p. 7)
test_conditions: Same simulated distribution for training and testing (N=256, 30 GHz); test sweeps over K=5-10, P, Rmin, alpha_N; classification tested at SNR 0-20 dB with noisy CSI (pp. 7-9)
baselines: Non-learned: capacity with dirty-paper coding [33], near-field NOMA [34], near-field LDMA [14] (polar codebook, ZF), far-field SDMA (DFT codebook). Learned: CNN [31], Transformer (p. 7)
metrics: Spectrum efficiency (sum rate) versus K, alpha_N, Rmin and P; far/near-field classification accuracy versus SNR; parameters, training and inference time (pp. 8-10)
complexity: Table II: 5.95M trainable and 129.56M total parameters; 59.92 ms training and 52.56 ms inference per batch of 100, compared with CNN and Transformer (p. 10)
openness: Simulation codes provided at http://oa.ee.tsinghua.edu.cn/dailinglong/publications/publications.html (footnote 2, p. 2); no dataset link
q1_support: p. 7: "to the channel model in [10], [32]". The channel is a custom near-field spherical-wave simulator (p. 3: "The Saleh-Valenzuela model" for the far-field part); 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data are never mentioned.
q2_support: p. 8: "directly applied to different number" of users is a capability claim only; the paper never states a K, antenna count, band or scenario in training that differs from testing. p. 7: "a testing dataset comprising 1,000 samples" built with the same channel model as training.
q3_support: p. 7: "(1) Capacity [33]" and "(4) Nearfield NOMA [34]" are non-learned; "(2) CNN [31]" and "(3) Transformer" are learned. p. 8: "outperforms other baselines for all user numbers" in spectrum efficiency (Fig. 6).
q4_support: p. 9: "as well as the computational complexity of the proposed" method is compared with DL baselines; Table II (p. 10) gives 5.95M/129.56M parameters and 59.92 ms training, 52.56 ms inference per batch.
q5_support: p. 2: "Simulation codes are provided to reproduce the results in this paper" with a link in footnote 2 (the authors' publications page, so the reviewer should confirm that the code is there).
notes: Area 3 chosen: the learned method is the precoder and power allocation of a terrestrial XL-MIMO BS (p. 3, Fig. 1); the UAVs are only users at heights up to 30 m (p. 7), with no satellite or aerial platform control, so area 6 is not assigned (reviewer may confirm). q2 is 0 because the number-of-users claim on p. 8 does not state training and test values that differ, and the SNR and CSI-noise sweeps (p. 8) do not count. q5 rests on the footnote link on p. 2, a general publications page of the group.
